matched_finding.subcategory: inadequate statistical power of original study and several replications
matched_finding.description: The original study had N=80, and several replications had similarly small samples (N=80, 81, 90, 90, 94). For detecting effects of r ≈ .20-.30 at 80% power with alpha = .05, approximately 95-197 participants are needed. The CREP minimum was set at 120, yet two studies had only 80 and 81 participants, and two had 90. The manuscript acknowledges this limitation but does not adequately address how underpowered individual studies affect the meta-analytic conclusions, particularly for the heterogeneity estimates.
matched_finding.quote: The CREP team specified the minimum sample size required for the replication; this size was generally set at the original study's sample size (which were small enough to be feasible for undergraduate student researchers, but set at 100 for larger studies). All studies in this meta-analysis received this approval by the CREP team, collected the minimum number of participants specified by the CREP (120 for the present study to ensure adequate statistical power)

ground_truth.modified_snippet: differences between the original and replication results might be related to variations in social media usage patterns across populations.

matched_finding.subcategory: temporal validity concern not adequately addressed
matched_finding.description: The authors note that Facebook's role as the primary social networking platform for young adults had changed between the original study (2012) and the replications (2016-2017), with Instagram and Snapchat becoming dominant. While this is mentioned as a possible explanation for divergent findings, the authors do not adequately grapple with the implication that the construct being measured (perceptions of Facebook relative to FTF) may have fundamentally changed in meaning for participants, making the replication a conceptually different study rather than a direct replication.
matched_finding.quote: both Snapchat and Instagram were among a new crop of social media outlets for US and UK participants that challenged Facebook as the preferred social networking site for the age cohort of the participants in this research

matched_finding.subcategory: no reporting of exclusion criteria or participant attrition
matched_finding.description: The manuscript does not report how many participants were recruited versus retained in each study, what exclusion criteria were applied (e.g., non-Facebook users, incomplete responses, attention check failures), or how many participants were excluded and why. Given that the study measures Facebook-specific perceptions, excluding non-Facebook users would be theoretically necessary but is never mentioned. This omission makes it impossible to assess selection bias within studies.
matched_finding.quote: Participants in all studies were undergraduate students at the five universities and colleges in the US where the replications were conducted from February, 2016 to June, 2017

ground_truth.original_snippet: We chose to use the restricted maximum likelihood (REML) model because it has been shown to exhibit less bias than the more commonly used DerSimonian and Laird (DL) model with small numbers of studies (Veroniki et al., 2016).
ground_truth.modified_snippet: We compared restricted maximum likelihood (REML) and DerSimonian and Laird (DL) models and selected REML as it produced more interpretable heterogeneity estimates for our data (Veroniki et al., 2016).
ground_truth.description: Changed principled REML selection (less bias with small k) to post-hoc model selection based on 'more interpretable' results — explicit analytic flexibility

matched_finding.description: The authors report that they 'compared restricted maximum likelihood (REML) and DerSimonian and Laird (DL) models and selected REML as it produced more interpretable heterogeneity estimates.' This model selection decision appears to have been made after examining the data, as the criterion ('more interpretable') is subjective and data-dependent. It is unclear whether this choice was pre-registered or made post-hoc, and the authors do not report what the DL results looked like, making it impossible to assess whether the choice affected conclusions.
matched_finding.quote: We compared restricted maximum likelihood (REML) and DerSimonian and Laird (DL) models and selected REML as it produced more interpretable heterogeneity estimates for our data
